facts.why: The shop in the film is Joe's Pizza. Mr. Aziz is the owner, not the name on the sign. The badge, the headline and the coupon all say AZIZ'S.
The real Joe's Pizza opened in 1975. The film gives no founding year, so 1962 is made up (a nod to Spider-Man's comic debut).
The only time limit I could confirm is Peter's 42 blocks in 7 and a half minutes. I could not open a source that shows a 29 minute promise in the film.

facts.text: LATE AGAIN 31 MINUTES. PIE IS FREE.
facts.why: Same problem as the 29 minute promise. The film's confirmed timing is 42 blocks in 7 and a half minutes. The 31 is not in any source I opened.
facts.fix: LATE AGAIN 8 MINUTES. PIE IS FREE.

facts.text: A stack of pies, one bungee cord, 42 blocks.
facts.why: The 42 blocks is right. I could not confirm a bungee cord holding the pies.
facts.fix: A stack of pies, 42 blocks, 7 and a half minutes.

facts.text: from the cart on Peter's walk to class
facts.why: No source I opened shows a knish cart on Peter's walk to class.
facts.fix: a hot knish on the run between jobs

vibe.verdict: Cheerful pizza coupon sheet built on the delivery run, but the shop name is wrong and the big moments from the film are thin.
missing: Pizza time! (Peter drops the pizza boxes on the desk)
42 blocks in 7 and a half minutes (Mr. Aziz)
Spider-Man webs a man's pizza out of his hands (street)
Octavius and the four tentacles at the fusion demo
Fighting Doc Ock on the subway train
Aunt May and the eviction notice
ideas: Swap the AZIZ'S badge for JOE'S and keep Mr. Aziz as the signature on the driver warning.
Swap the 29 MINUTES burst for 42 BLOCKS, 7 1/2 MINUTES.
Swap the 'Costume party?' line for a PIZZA TIME stamp across the coupon.
Replace 'Cheese pie, Eight big slices' note with 'Webbed to your hand, no charge'.
